# aeneid-046 — new house renderings

No new house renderings. No set piece on the pending list falls in VI.608–702.

For the reviewer (not proposed as house renderings), the best-known lines of the part, built from the Latin alone:

- VI.620 *Discite iustitiam moniti, et non temnere divos.* (Phlegyas; single marks, inside the Sibyl's speech)
  - `l`: "‘Learn justice, being warned, and not to despise the gods.’"
  - `i`: "‘Take warning, all of you: learn to be just, and learn not to hold the gods in contempt.’"
  - Deliberately avoided the common "Be warned, learn justice, and do not scorn the gods" shape. (Review: the drafter's "not to slight the gods" was itself a known version's wording; rephrased.)
- VI.625–627 *Non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, / ferrea vox…*
  - `l`: "No, if I had tongues a hundred and mouths a hundred, / a voice of iron, all the forms of crimes to take in, / all the names of punishments to run through, I could not.”"
  - `i`: "No: were I given a hundred tongues and as many mouths, and a voice of iron, even so I could not compass every form their crimes have taken, nor tell over every name of their punishments.”"
  - Avoided Dryden's "Had I a hundred mouths, a hundred tongues" and the "Not if I had a hundred tongues…" opening.
- VI.700–702 *Ter conatus ibi collo dare brachia circum…* (= II.792–794)
  - `l`: "Thrice he tried there to his neck to give arms around, / thrice in vain grasped from the hands escaped the image, / [equal to light winds and most like to a winged sleep.]"
  - `i`: "Three times he tried, there, to throw his arms around his father's neck; three times the image, grasped in vain, slipped from his hands, [as light as the breezes and most like a sleep that flies.]"
  - Kept to aeneid-016's rendering of II.792–794, changed only to third person and "his father's neck"; line 702 bracketed as Greenough prints it.
